<thought>Based on the molecular formula C8H15O4Cl (DBE = 1, no aromatic carbons, two methyl groups, one carbonyl, and a chlorine), the molecule can be thought of as a chlorinated alkyl chain attached to an ester fragment. A reasonable way to split it into two joinable pieces is a chlorobutyl fragment and an acetate‑propyl fragment. Their SMILES strings are “ClCCCC” (chlorobutyl) and “C(=O)OCCC” (propyl acetate). Joining these two fragments at the carbon bearing the chlorine gives a structure that matches the overall formula and functional‑group count.</thought>
<final_answer>['ClCCCC', 'C(=O)OCCC']</final_answer>
